title: Transfer: a lazy reader for the station log

blocks.promptMd: What does `for line in handle:` iterate over for an open text file?

choices.md: Its lines, one at a time, without loading the file

blocks.explainMd: A text file object implements the iterator protocol over lines, so it is already a lazy stream and can be the first stage of a pipeline. `readlines()` is the eager alternative: it hands back a list of every line, which is the one thing you were trying to avoid.

blocks.promptMd: You return `temps(records(handle))` from inside the `with` and call `sum()` on it afterwards. What happens?

choices.md: It works — the generator kept the data
`ValueError`: the file was closed before the pipeline read it

blocks.explainMd: The pipeline had not read anything yet, so the reading happens after `__exit__` has closed the handle. Laziness means the work moves to wherever you consume it — so consume inside the block, or have the manager itself yield finished values rather than an open handle.

blocks.promptMd: In one or two sentences: which part of your reader guarantees the file closes, and which part guarantees the log is never all in memory at once?

> Build the reader over `station.log`. `opened(path)` is a `@contextmanager` that closes the file even when the block raises. `records(lines)` yields each line stripped, skipping blanks and `#` comments. `temps(rows)` yields the integer from every `temp=` row. Output should be `12`.

hintLadder.md: Both stages return empty lists today, so the total is 0. The log is read-only — read it, do not rewrite it.
`records`: strip the line, `continue` on an empty line or one starting with `#`, otherwise `yield` it. `temps`: split each row once on `=` and `yield int(value)` when the left side is `temp`.
`kind, _, value = row.partition("=")` splits `"temp=4"` into `"temp"`, `"="`, `"4"` and leaves a row with no `=` sign as `("bad line", "", "")`, which the `if` then skips.

description: Read a log too big to hold, one record at a time.
